title: Staged GPU allocation playbook: tenant overlays and phased releases
body:
Purpose:
Small working-sheet to coordinate staggered releases of Dedicated GPU reservations across regions for high-touch customers. This focuses on overlays (temporary bursts) and phased handover from hosted to dedicated for customers onboarding Q3–Q4 2029.

Summary (one-liner):
Provide a low-friction cadence for releasing contracted slabs, ensure per-region utilization targets, and keep a rolling 20% pool for emergency rebalancing.

Key assumptions:
- Primary SKUs: H100-80GB (h100-80), A100-40GB (a100-40), L4-48GB (l4-48) are available in US-W, US-E, EU-C, AP-SE regions.
- Contract reservations are billed monthly and can be phased across a 6–12 month window.
- Target steady-state utilization per slab: 68% (to leave headroom for burst and KV-cache warmups).
- Operational buffer: 20% of reserved GPUs per region as rebalancing capacity.

Utilization monitoring plan:
- Forward-looking: daily 1:00 UTC sampling of per-route token/tps to estimate upcoming 24h demand.
- Alert thresholds: sustained >85% allocated GPU utilization for 2 hours -> paging to infra oncall.
- Regression checks: customer QoS dropped >10% after handover -> automatic rollback (can re-pin to hosted variant).

Operational buffer and rebalancing rules:
- Keep a hot pool equal to max(20% of regional reserved GPUs, 8 GPUs).
- Rebalancing window: up to 48 hours for cross-region moves, up to 6 hours for intra-region slab reassignments.
- Priority order for buffer usage: emergency SLA breach customers -> onboarding customer ramp -> short-term bursts.

Risk register (top 5):
- R1: SKU shortage (H100) in target region -> contingency: failover to A100 with quantized model variant; trigger capacity-skew runbook (JIRA-INFRA-1123).
- R2: KV cache warm-up causing latency spikes on day 1 -> mitigation: pre-warm with synthetic traffic 12h before handover.
- R3: Customer usage exceeds forecast causing knock-on impact to other tenants -> mitigation: temporary rate-limits + notify customer success for rapid communication.
- R4: Networking or transitive cost mismatch for private deployments -> mitigation: early cost-sim with customer network team and staged egress sampling.
- R5: Billing reconciliation drift for partial-month releases -> mitigation: standardize on pro-rated slab-lines and run weekly reconciliation script.

Open action items:
- [A1] Diego to run pre-warm synthetic load for RC-7582 on 2029-07-07 (ticket: JIRA-INFRA-1332).
- [A2] Maya to prepare A/B latency test harness for EU-C initial release by 2029-08-01.
- [A3] Oliver to confirm AP-SE H100 availability and fallback mapping to a100-40 by 2029-09-01.
- [A4] Finance: publish pro-rate billing example tables for partial-month reservations (link in linked_artifacts).

Notes from customer success sync (2029-06-28):
- NovusAI requests the ability to burst an extra 32 GPUs for two 2-hour windows per week in month 1; agreed to allow within operational buffer if not in conflict.
- HealthFlow requires SOC2 attestation on the private control plane before full claim; move full claim to conditional state until receipt.

Decision log (summary):
- 2029-06-21: Agreed to standard 20% buffer across regions, except AP-SE where we hold 25% due to regional procurement variability.
- 2029-06-30: Approved staged release pattern for RC-7582 to avoid noisy-neighbor risk on day 1.

Appendix: quick reference commands and tickets
- Rebalance workflow: gh pr create --title "rebalance/region/US-W->EU-C" -b "temporary reassign for RC-XXXX" (see GIT-PR-branch/reservation-optimizer)
- Capacity query: infraql "SELECT sku,count FROM reservations WHERE region='US-W' GROUP BY sku"
